set.st: An unidentified vessel said to carry $4.5 million in gold bullion sank near Poverty Island. Dunathan (1953) judged it less grounded than the Sand Bay story. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. The story was already being chased in 1933: the schooner Captain Lawrence, carrying an amateur diving party from Milwaukee and Muskegon, wrecked in a gale off Fayette on 21 September 1933 while seeking 'treasure lost years ago between Poverty Island and Middle Gull Island'; the party would not say what or where (Escanaba Daily Press, 21 Sep 1933). That is the earliest print found and the only placement: the water between Poverty Island and the Gull Islands to its north-west.
set.t: Underwater; look-only for the atlas. Access: water. Earliest print found: 1933 (salvage attempt); nothing earlier.
pinev: Placed from the source text: GNIS Poverty Island
1933 report narrows the search zone to the strait between Poverty Island and the Gull Islands; pin stays on Poverty Island.

src: Escanaba Daily Press, 21 Sep 1933, p. 3 (Captain Lawrence wreck, treasure hunt)
